newsitem.title: USA: Brazil bond drew wide global interest - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil bond drew wide global interest - JP Morgan.

text.p: Brazil's deal to swap Brady bonds for new 30-year global bonds priced Wednesday drew strong interest from investors across the world, said co-lead manager J.P. Morgan on Wednesday.

"We had people coming to the tender from every single point of the world," said Andres Rojo, head of emerging markets syndicate at Morgan. "We had good demand from the U.S., Europe, Asia and Latin America."
Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan acted as lead managers for the swap/buyback offer that was announced in May.

Brazil on Wednesday priced $3.0 billion of 30-year global bonds at 395 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries, including $1.622 billion in principal amount for discount bonds, $542 million for pars and $86 million for Cs.
Brazil also sold $750 million of the global bond outright for cash. The amount sold was dwarfed by the $16 billion in bids received, most of them non-competitive.
In its offer last month, Brazil limited the size of cash purchases to 25 percent of the total size of the global issue.
"On the new cash (purchase), we had a tremendous amount of crossover, non-traditional buyers, mainly U.S. institutions," Rojo said. "The amount of new buyers for Brazil has been tremendous."
There were 650 participants in the offer, Rojo said.
"Brazil banks had an interest, but if you had to judge by size they have not been the main factor," Rojo said. "They were even with other types of investors."

Brazil also said it would purchase $652,500 in principal amount of par bonds and $871,500 in principal amount of discount bonds for cash, at prices equal to $653.40 per $1,000 principal amount of pars and $818.75 per $1,000 principal amount of discounts.
The principal amount of Global Bonds issued for each $1,000 in original principal amount of Brady Bonds exchanged was $700.82 for par bonds, $878.17 for discounts and $941.52, for C bonds.
